(master plan `docs/research/fable51_next_push_master_plan_2026-09-27.md` §W1.4, §3.1 A10, §3.9 N3, §6.8).

**Fix round (2026-09-28, section 8).** Reviewers raised 18 problems. Section 8 records the verdict on each,
the fixes and the re-run gates; where the text below was wrong it is corrected in place and marked
"(fix round)". In short: every frontier stop now reports a paused session (a loop-exit case did not); the
swap stop watches the campaign's own swap, not host-wide swap-in; host-wide stops count toward the
liveness refusal only when attributed to the campaign; the admitted RAM cap rule is stated and recorded;
N3 is **implemented, its registered gate open**; the lane binaries were rebuilt from committed source with
provenance sidecars and re-validated on C-5F, four-all, the per-family four-loop controls, the drills
and the oracle.

## 0. In brief

- **A10 frontier stop** is implemented natively (`--frontier-policy record|stop`), bound into CP5 only
  for `stop` (existing checkpoints and record receipts unchanged), wired through the thin driver,
  supervisor, monitor and production launcher (new campaigns default to `stop`). Drill on the FG frontier
  fixture: 13 stops at the 13 frontier records, final result strict-identical to the record walk [M].
  (fix round) A stop on initial input frontiers with an empty worklist, or on the walk's last commit,
  ended as an "incomplete" document with `resume_supported: false`; every frontier stop is now a paused,
  resumable session (exit 4).
- **Host-aware RAM guard** in `shared_owner_campaign.py`: cooperative save-and-stop on RSS soft limit, on
  host MemAvailable at the floor (**default 50 GB**, owner decision; configurable) and (fix round) on
  sustained growth of the campaign's own swapped-out memory (host-wide swap-in is telemetry only); hard
  stop at a quarter of the floor; ZFS ARC and swap telemetry; production liveness guard (host-wide stops
  count only when attributed to the campaign). Admission keeps the floor free: the effective hard cap is
  `min(requested, MemAvailable - 50 GB)` at every (re)start, so 600 GB needs 650 GB MemAvailable.
- **Flaky tests**: the two named in the handoff plus the core catalog test run isolated in their own
  process; a contention stress found and fixed two more (`cli::shards` ETXTBSY, a Ready `run_pause` race

- **License gates**: every license-gated test prints a visible skip marker, `RUSTRED_TESTS_REQUIRE_LICENSE=1`

## 1. A10: `--frontier-policy {record,stop}`

- `FrontierPolicy` (`walking/work_policy.rs`): `Record` (default, the historical behaviour) keeps walking
  past committed frontiers; `Stop` saves the checkpoint and stops cooperatively (exit 4, stop reason
  `frontier_policy`) at the first frontier the session commits. Frontiers stay explicit, persisted and
  blocking certification under both policies; only continuation differs.
- Trigger: the committed frontier count at session start (0 for a fresh walk, so initial input frontiers
  stop it before any inspection; the restored count on resume). It fires at most once per session, at a
  checkpoint opportunity, and persists exactly the state that contains the new frontier's record (forced
  final save labelled `stop_reason: frontier_policy` in the manifest metadata), journals a
  `frontier_stop` event, then cancels like a stop request. Resuming is the operator's explicit decision
  to continue to the next new frontier.
- Binding: `Stop` is bound into the CP5 request binding; `Record` adds no key, so every existing CP5
  checkpoint and control keeps its digest (a test restates the pre-A10 formula and compares digests).
  A Stop checkpoint refuses a Record resume and vice versa. Record receipts are byte-identical (no new
  keys); Stop receipts add `frontier_policy` and, when fired, `stop_reason`.
- Admission: Stop requires a checkpointed Ordered or Ready walk.
- CLI `rustred owner-domain-match --follow-successors --frontier-policy {record,stop}` (stop needs
  `--checkpoint` or `--resume`); thin Python driver
  `match_shared_owner_domains.py` (requires `--follow-successors` and a checkpoint); supervisor
  `shared_owner_campaign.py` forwards and records it (request, status, summary, resume command; the
  monitor shows `PAUSED · stop frontier_policy`); the production launcher freezes `stop` for new
  campaigns (steering schema v3) and keeps `record` for steering written before the option existed.
- The CLI journal (`--events`) records `frontier_stop` as a milestone next to the checkpoint events (the
  first drill found it dropped by the journal's event allow-list; fixed, with a unit test).

Tests [M]: `tests/frontier_policy.rs` (5: Ordered stop at each new frontier and resume to the record result

## 2. Host-aware RAM guard (`shared_owner_campaign.py`)

`RamGuard` is a pure state machine over /proc readings (tests drive it with fake readers).

| Trigger | Kind | Default |
|---|---|---|
| aggregate RSS of the supervised tree reaches soft = hard x (1 - margin) | cooperative save-and-stop (exit 4) | margin 5% |
| host (or enclosing cgroup) MemAvailable falls to the floor | cooperative save-and-stop | **floor 50 GB** |
| (fix round) growth of the supervised tree's own swapped-out memory (`VmSwap` summed over its processes) at or above a rate in every sample for a window (`own_swap_growth_sustained`); host-wide swap-in (`/proc/vmstat pswpin`) is recorded only | cooperative save-and-stop | 32 MiB/s for 120 s (0 disables) |
| RSS reaches hard, or MemAvailable falls to a quarter of the floor | SIGKILL of the owned native | 12.5 GB emergency |

- **Floor default (owner decision 2026-09-27): a flat 50 GB** (`DEFAULT_HOST_MEMORY_RESERVE_BYTES`),
  replacing `min(20 GB, 5% of host/cgroup RAM)`. It is configurable with `--host-memory-reserve-bytes`
  (alias `--host-available-floor-bytes`). Admission leaves the floor free; a host or cgroup with less
  than the floor available is refused with a message naming the flag, so small hosts must pass an
  explicit floor. The production launcher freezes the 50 GB value explicitly into new steering and it
  may be overridden per resume like the other RAM options; steering frozen before the option existed
  gets the supervisor default (now also 50 GB).
- Every resource sample records MemAvailable, the ZFS ARC size (`arcstats size`, counted as used by the
  kernel and shrinkable to `c_min`), the swap-in rate and sustained seconds, and the native's `VmSwap`;
  the summary records the policy, the initial host snapshot, the minimum observed MemAvailable and the
  maximum observed ARC.
- Liveness: the production launcher refuses `--resume` after `--max-zero-progress-ram-stops` (default 2)
  consecutive RAM-guard stops without committed progress (the legacy walk has no per-ID attempt counter,
  so a head whose inspection alone trips the guard would otherwise loop).

Tests [M]: `examples/python/test_ram_guard_frontier_policy.py` (13: fake /proc readers, the guard state
machine and its validation, the 50 GB default and an explicit floor, a supervised fake native stopped by
sustained swap-in, the frontier stop forwarded and reported, thin-driver validation, production steering
v3 and legacy steering, liveness streaks and the refused looping resume); admission expectations in
`test_shared_owner_campaign.py` updated to the 50 GB floor. Python suite: 239 tests OK, 1 skipped.

## 3. Timing-flaky tests

Isolated runs did not reproduce the handoff's flakes (baseline binary under 16 nice-19 burners:
`cli::shards` x200 and `ready_late_native_fault...` x200, 0 failures [M]). Equal-priority contention did:
12 concurrent test processes on the 16 lane CPUs for 600 s (`TMP/ops/contend.sh`) [M]:

| filter (4 loops each) | baseline e6a2c23c (runs / failures) | hardened (runs / failures) |
|---|---|---|
| `cli::shards` | 5,066 / 7 (ETXTBSY at `launch().unwrap()`; fix round: 5,068 was a miscount) | 5,028 / 0 |
| `walking::execution::ready` | 1,349 / 211 (`ready_changed_parked_prefix_fails_before_any_suffix_admission`, left 18 right 17) | 1,230 / 0 |
| `walking::parallel` | 8,645 / 0 | 8,527 / 0 |

Run directories `TMP/ops/contend-baseline/` and `TMP/ops/contend-step3/` (worktree `TMP/`).

- `crate::test_gates::isolated(path)` (app and core): the parent test re-executes the test binary filtered to
  exactly that test (`--exact --test-threads=1`), requires `1 passed`, forwards the child's skip markers, and
  returns; the child runs the body with no sibling in the process.
- `orphan_child_retains_campaign_lock_until_exit` and the four `cli::shards` tests that write and exec a fake
  executable run isolated: a sibling that forks while this test holds a descriptor keeps a copy until its own
  exec, so a released lock can stay held and exec of the just-written fake fails with ETXTBSY.
- `persistence::catalog::tests::arbitrary_exact_expressions_roundtrip_with_deduplicated_values` (core) runs
  isolated: the partial Symbolica state export appends every variable list and finite field registered since
  the state offset, so a sibling registering one between the two encodings changes the bytes.
- `ready_late_native_fault_after_cancellation_disallows_pause`: the other tickets wait until ticket 0 is inside
  its visitor, so a later commit (hence a checkpoint callback) always observes it and cancels.
- `ready_changed_parked_prefix_fails_before_any_suffix_admission` / `run_pause` (a flake the contention run
  found, 15.6 % of runs): the pause predicate also requires all 18 domains admitted, and tickets >= 2 wait until
  tickets 0 and 1 have emitted their prefixes; before, a mounted ticket >= 2 with an accepted Count event could
  be paused on together with one of tickets 0/1.

## 4. License-gated tests (review #17, plan §6.8)

- `crate::test_gates::licensed_or_skip(test)` (app and core) replaces every silent
  `if !LicenseManager::is_licensed() { return; }` gate in test code (35 gate calls in 12 files, the local
  `licensed(test)` helper of the parallel tests included). The owner-batches driver test already asserts the
  license and so fails without it. Without a license the gate writes
  `SKIPPED <test>: SYMBOLICA_LICENSE absent ...; the test exercised nothing and passes vacuously` to the real
  stderr (past libtest's capture, so it shows in every suite run); `test_gates::skip` does the same for the
  other vacuous gates (fewer than 2 cores, workers unavailable).
- `crate::test_gates::workers_or_skip(test, workers)` (app and core) gates the W>1 variants of worker-loop
  tests on the host core-budget preflight: when the preflight fails for lack of the license it goes through
  `licensed_or_skip`; otherwise it skips visibly with the preflight error (e.g. W50 on a 16-CPU affinity mask).
  It replaces preflight gates that bypassed strict mode (owner-batches and frontier-policy worker helpers,
  delegation control, refined-successor subdivision) and seven that were fully silent (three in
  `tests/parallel_walk.rs`, two of them whole tests; `native_walk_cancellation_at_alias...`;
  `initial_overlap_actual_native_residual...`; and core `k6_wave` x2, both whole tests).
- Strict mode: `RUSTRED_TESTS_REQUIRE_LICENSE=1` turns every license skip into a failure. Plan §6.8 asks that
  epoch soundness tests fail rather than skip without the license; those tests do not exist yet (W2), so the
  mechanism is the opt-in variable plus the gate helpers for them to call.
- Without the license, an unfiltered suite does not pass vacuously [M, `TMP/ops/nolicense-step3/`]: the
  multi-threaded runs of both lib suites abort (SIGABRT) because unlicensed Symbolica aborts when used from a
  second thread; single-threaded, the core suite still aborts at an ungated test that spawns its own threads
  (`concurrent_context_construction_reuses_deterministic_positional_symbols`), and the app suite reports
  28 failures (ungated tests that need the license, e.g. the owner-batches driver tests, which assert it).
  Pre-existing behaviour, unchanged here.
- Gate check [M] (`TMP/ops/nolicense-gates-step4/results.txt`): each of the 42 gated tests run alone
  (`--exact --test-threads=1`) without `SYMBOLICA_LICENSE`: all 42 pass with a visible SKIPPED marker by
  default, and all 42 fail under `RUSTRED_TESTS_REQUIRE_LICENSE=1`. Before `workers_or_skip`, 12 of the
  then 35 gated tests still passed in strict mode (`TMP/ops/nolicense-gates/`).

## 5. N3: `[profile.campaign]` and mimalloc

- `[profile.campaign]` in the workspace `Cargo.toml`: `inherits = "release"`, `lto = "fat"`,
  `codegen-units = 1`. No `target-cpu`: W0.8 measured znver4 at x0.95-1.09, no gain.
  `cargo build --profile campaign --locked --offline -p rustred-app --bin rustred` -> `target/campaign/rustred`.
- Feature `mimalloc` of `rustred-app` (opt-in, off by default): `mimalloc` 0.1.52 with `override` as the
  `rustred` binary's `#[global_allocator]`; the override also replaces the process's C `malloc` family, so
  GMP/MPFR allocations (through C malloc, no `set_memory_functions` in the tree) use it too. Verified [M]:
  `nm -D` of the mimalloc binary shows `malloc` and `free` defined (`T`); release and plain campaign import
  them. `Cargo.lock` gains only `mimalloc` 0.1.52 and `libmimalloc-sys` 0.1.49 (both in the offline cache).
- Binaries [M] (`TMP/w1-ops/bin/`, sha256 prefix in the name; fix round: superseded by the r2 binaries of 8.2,
  whose sidecars record their source): `rustred-ops-release-25906f1a`,
  `rustred-ops-campaign-c6d5d7b4`, `rustred-ops-campaign-mimalloc-2f4de0b5`, all from this branch's final
  non-test source. A fat-LTO single-unit build of `rustred` took about 64 min under host load.

## 8. Fix round (2026-09-28)

Reviewers raised 18 problems (two pairs overlap). Each was checked against the code and the run directories
before acting; none was a false positive. Commits on `fable_5_1-v3-ops`: `2164dcb3` (A10 paused fix, test
pins, Cargo.toml comment), `704724cb` (build lock check, provenance), `13dce0ef` (RAM guard), `fc3c07e4` and
`1d66b837` (gate tooling), plus this note.

### 8.1 Verdicts and fixes

| # | Problem (severity) | Verdict | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| P6 | frontier stop before the run loop ends "incomplete", `resume_supported: false` (minor, [E]) | real (code: the loop never observes the cancellation when the worklist is empty, and also on the walk's last commit, where `next == len` ends the loop) | `walking/mod.rs`: after the checkpointed run, `checkpoint_paused = true` whenever this session's frontier stop fired; the final save records `paused` (in the change stamp). Tests: the input-frontier test now asserts `paused`/`resume_supported` and resumes to the end; new `frontier_stop_on_the_last_commit_reports_a_paused_session` (precondition: the only frontier record is the last record) |
| P11 | no test pins the stop to the first new frontier (minor) | real | unit test: each stop's journal event and final state lie in the next frontier record of the Ordered record walk (frontier count in (F_{k-1}, F_k], committed domains i_k or i_k+1; one more commit fails); drill: the same pin per session against the fixture, plus the exact-match count |
| P3 | host-wide swap-in stop (minor) | real | the stop watches the supervised tree's own `VmSwap` growth (`own_swap_growth_sustained`, same 32 MiB/s x 120 s defaults, options renamed `--swap-growth-stop-*`); `pswpin` is telemetry; host-wide stops carry an attribution (`own_memory_signal`: tree RSS growth >= 50% of the MemAvailable drop over the window, or own swap growing) and count toward the liveness refusal only with it |
| P4 | admitted cap `min(hard, MemAvailable - 50 GB)` unstated (minor) | real | stated here, in the driver doc and the report; `memory_admission` (rule, MemAvailable, ARC, floor, effective hard/soft, `hard_capped_by_available_memory`) in request/status/summary; a stderr line when the cap is reduced; `memory_admission_preview` in the production plan (`active-run.json`). Decoupling admission from the floor is left to the owner (D item below) |

| C-5F W50 | campaign+mimalloc | 2 | 0.832 | 1.4% | 0.823 (all below) | 1.035 | 1.104 | 0.44-0.51 |

Release references (same sessions): instructions per native 3.98 M (FG), 5.63 M (BMW), 15.48 M (H), 18.92 M (X),
10.66 M (C-5F); inspector CPU 0.325 / 0.484 / 1.500 / 1.907 / 0.964 ms per native; peak RSS 0.267 / 0.462 /
0.516 / 0.929 / 6.549 GB (tables: `TMP/w1-ops/runs/n3r2-summary.json`, `n3r2c5f-summary.json`).

- `[profile.campaign]` removes 5.6-7.3% of the instructions per native on all five controls, reproducibly; its
  CPU-time ratios agree in direction but overlap release on FG, BMW and H at n = 3. Peak RSS is unchanged.
- The mimalloc feature on top removes 16.8-22.2% of the instructions per native in total, and its CPU per
  native lies below every release run on every control. Its IPC moves both ways (x0.92-1.06), and it costs
  peak RSS: +2.5..+20% on C-4L, +10.4% (+0.68 GB of 6.55 GB) on C-5F.
- [E] Against the W0.8 build gate (>= 5% less inspector CPU per native with strict identity) both arms pass in
  instructions; in inspector CPU only mimalloc is clear of release everywhere. Against the registered W1.2
  gate the harness part is open (8.4). The instruction and CPU counts include the preparation phase; their
  ratios are therefore conservative for the native phase. These are 1-6 minute controls: the gen-7 cost mix
  (hot owner 64% of Apply CPU) is not represented (handoff 0.1 item 7), which the harness part addresses.

(the samples after the stop request are the save and teardown), output `TMP/ops/rss-fit-s3.jsonl` (worktree).

| arm | natives in 45 min | discovered domains at stop | marginal RSS per discovered domain, second half | R^2 | peak RSS | RSS at 1M / 2M / 3M / 4M / 4.7M discovered domains | instr/native | foreign load |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| campaign | 2,720,290 | 4,770,410 | 509 B (3.01M-4.77M domains) | 0.994 | 8.22 GB | 6.47 / 6.90 / 7.38 / 7.88 / 8.21 GB | 25.87 M | 0.27 |
| campaign+mimalloc | 3,215,994 | 5,369,561 | 411 B (3.34M-5.37M domains) | 0.955 | 9.20 GB | 7.10 / 7.57 / 7.94 / 8.44 / 8.82 GB | 23.07 M | 0.25 |

(RSS at matched domain counts: maximum over the samples within 1% of the count.) Ordered publication makes the
two arms' domain sequences identical, so the comparison at matched discovered domains is like for like; the
arms ran concurrently on different nodes, which perturbs their speed, not their RSS per domain.

- [M] At matched discovered domains the mimalloc arm holds +0.50 to +0.67 GB more (x1.07-1.10), an offset
  that does not grow with the domain count over 1M-4.7M; its marginal per domain is not higher (411 vs 509 B,
  the mimalloc curve is noisier because the allocator returns memory in bursts). Its instructions per native
  are x0.892 of the plain campaign arm on this owner and it inspected 18% more natives in the same wall time.
- [E] On this evidence the mimalloc RAM cost at W48 is a fixed per-process/per-thread offset of about 0.6 GB,
  not a multiplier on the ~0.5 KB/domain marginal that sets the 600 GB wall. W0.8's +29..+72% at W48 was the
  same kind of offset measured on 0.3-1.4 GB controls. Not covered: the aged regime (a gen-7, 74M-domain
  resume), W100 (twice the threads, so twice any per-thread offset), and restore VmHWM.

### 8.4 What stays open for N3 (the registered gate) [M/E]

- **Harness K=1 and K=96** (W1.2: >= 20% less inspector CPU per native in the 0.3 harness) was not run for the
  compiled N3 binaries. The harness is a test-binary mode of branch `fable_5_1-v3-harness` (`reinspection.rs`),
  absent from this branch; measuring the compiled profile and allocator needs the harness built with
  `[profile.campaign]` (and `--features mimalloc`), i.e. after the merge train or on a scratch merge. Existing
  evidence [M, harness lane, `docs/research/fable51_w0_harness_2026-09-27.md` sections 5-7]: mimalloc through
  `LD_PRELOAD` gives x0.963 / x0.978 CPU per native at K=96 (n=2) and is unresolved at K=1 within the 3.5% base
  noise, with instructions per native constant across K. [E] On that evidence mimalloc alone does not approach
  the 20% bar and does not change the scaling; its per-thread heaps do not remove the per-operation refcount
  and shared-counter writes that orchestrator decision 2 names as the root cause.
- **RSS at campaign width**: the fix-round C-HOT W48 pilot (8.3b) shows a ~0.6 GB offset and no higher marginal;
  a gen-7 (aged, 74M-domain) resume at W100 with each arm, the directive 0.1.7 "aged pilot" with restore
  VmHWM, was not run (two 50-min socket-1 slots).
- Until both close, mimalloc stays out of every launch arm; `[profile.campaign]` is separable (RSS neutral,
  instructions x0.93) and can be decided on its own.

### 8.5 Owner-visible items and follow-ups

- **RAM admission (D item).** With the owner's 50 GB floor, admission keeps the floor free: the effective hard
  cap is `min(600 GB, MemAvailable - 50 GB)` at every start and resume, 586-600 GB for the handoff's
  636-692 GB MemAvailable (soft 556.7-570 GB at the 5% margin), and it is recorded (`memory_admission`) and
  previewed by the launcher. A pure runtime floor (admission on MemAvailable plus the ARC above `c_min`, minus
  the floor) would keep 600 GB at lower MemAvailable; not implemented, owner decision.
- **Host-wide stop attribution.** The 50% share and the window (the swap window, 120 s) are the lane's choice
  [E]; they only decide whether a host-wide stop counts toward the zero-progress resume refusal.
- **Supervisor label.** A walk that ends incomplete with explicit frontiers exits 4 without a pause and the
  supervisor labels it `failed` (pre-existing). Under the stop policy that is the normal end of the session
  after the last frontier; a distinct `incomplete` state is suggested, not changed here.
- **Oracle and A10.** The oracle binary predates `--frontier-policy`, so Stop checkpoints are verified on a
  binding-substituted copy (negative control recorded); after the oracle and ops branches meet, verify them
  directly.
- Still open from the lane: the off-pool copy (waits for W0.10); `independent_owner_campaign.py` keeps its
  20 GB host reserve in the `cli::shards` config; epoch soundness tests (W2) should use the license gates.
